blocks.text: Where an economist's working day goes

An economist's week is a mix of thinking, typing and talking. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics lists the core duties as research, collecting data through surveys, analyzing data with mathematical models and statistical software, forecasting, advising, and presenting results in tables, graphs and articles. Each of those tasks lives in a different app on your Mac.

The sources checked for this page do not measure how economists split their time. The BLS page gives no time-use figures for the job. So the numbers below come from office workers in general. Treat them as a rough guide, not a count of your own week.

Microsoft's 2023 Work Trend Index used Microsoft 365 telemetry from a 28-day period ending March 2023. The heaviest email users, the top 25%, spent 8.8 hours a week on email. The heaviest meeting users spent 7.5 hours a week in meetings. The report excludes education customers.

Across the workforce, Microsoft reports an average split of 57% communicating and 43% creating. Communicating covers meetings, email and chat. That split matters for you. The analysis you were hired to do sits in the 43% slice, and the rest can fill the week fast.
Measure your own week before you change anything

Start with the Mac's own data. Open System Settings > Screen Time and read which apps took the most time this week. Then sort your tasks into these groups: analysis, writing, email and meetings, and admin. The group that surprises you is your first target.

items: Note every task you repeat more than once a week. Those are your best candidates for a voice request.
Count how often you look up the same Excel formula or Stata option. Repeat lookups are a good sign a voice question will save time.
Mark the emails that needed a reply within the hour. Those show how fast your inbox really moves.
Write the totals on paper. Compare them with the same check next month.

blocks.text: Which apps take up an economist's Mac

Your Mac probably runs a handful of apps for this job. Excel and Word for Mac, Outlook or Apple Mail, Chrome, and a statistics package such as Stata are the usual set. Lazur sees whichever app is in front of you, so the same shortcut works in each one.

Microsoft's release notes list Version 16.114.3 (Build 26102720) as the latest Office for Mac release, dated October 27, 2026. Its only listed fix covers an update that inadvertently disabled Office 2021 for existing users. Outlook for Mac changed a lot in 2026, with a reorderable left rail and Liquid Glass styling. The same notes list no ribbon changes, so the Excel and Word menus you know should still be there.

Stata is not an Apple app, but it runs on Macs. StataCorp's Mac page offers Stata 19 and asks you to run the latest update. It supports macOS 13 (Ventura) through 26 (Tahoe) on Apple silicon, and macOS 10.13 (High Sierra) through 26 (Tahoe) on Intel. Check that page before you upgrade macOS.
What Lazur does on your Mac

Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and it draws a circle and a label around that spot. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. You do the clicking. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you.

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots save the phrases you type every week. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report.
Excel help for economists: pivot tables and messy data

Excel is a common place to clean data, so start there. A typical problem is a panel with dates stored as text. Sorting goes wrong, and a pivot table treats each date as a label. The fix takes only a few steps, and Lazur can walk you through each one.

items: Select the date column. Read the alignment. Text sits on the left, and real dates sit on the right by default.
Go to Data > Text to Columns. Finish the wizard with a Date format for the column.
Click any cell in the data, then go to Insert > PivotTable. Choose a new worksheet.
Drag state into Rows and the rate into Values. Click the arrow in Values and choose Average, not Sum.

blocks.text: Say your sheet has one row per county per month. You want the mean unemployment rate by state. The Sum default gives a total that means nothing for a rate. Average is the right summary, so change it before you read a single number.

Watch for blanks and text values. A pivot table skips blank cells, so an average can drop missing rows without warning. Check the count next to the average. If the count is lower than you expect, look for text entries in the rate column.
Ask Lazur for help at any step. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and say, Lazur, how do I set this field to average? Lazur circles the setting and waits while you click.
Word for economists: tables, equations and tracked edits

Word holds the working paper, and co-authors send it back with edits. Turn on tracking before you send the file. Go to Review > Track Changes. When changes come back, ask Lazur what each one does before you accept it.
Two Word menus matter most for economists. Use Insert > Equation for formulas. Use Review > Compare to check what changed between two drafts. Ask Lazur to point at either one when you cannot find it.
Dictation saves time on prose. Hold fn in the open paper and speak a paragraph. Then read it. Check every symbol and equation by eye, because voice input can mishear them.

blocks.title: Mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not accept a tracked change you do not understand. Ask Lazur to explain it first. Then accept it, reject it or reply in the margin.
Stata questions without leaving your do-file

A Stata error can stop a whole run. Keep the error visible and hold ⌥ ⌘. Ask what the message means. Lazur reads the text on screen and explains it out loud, in plain English. It can also point at the part of the screen that matches the error.

Lazur does not run your do-file, and it does not edit your code. Paste any fix yourself, run the file, and check the output against what you expected. For a model choice, use Lazur to explain a command's syntax. The model choice stays yours.
Stata's own documentation is the reference for syntax. Use the Stata for Mac page to confirm your version and macOS support before you update either one.
Email and meetings: getting time back

Email is the easiest place to win back time. Lazur only looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut. Inside a message, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask for a short reply in your own tone. Then read it before you send it.

Apple's Mail guide describes automatic sorting into Primary, Transactions, Updates and Promotions. It also describes Writing Tools that summarize and proofread. The guide targets macOS 27, and availability varies by language and region. Check your Mac's version before you rely on a feature.

Use voice for the follow-up. Say, Lazur, remind me to send the table to Ana on Friday. Lazur adds the reminder to Apple Reminders. Calendar events and timers work the same way, so you do not switch apps to log a task.

Outlook users see a different layout. Microsoft's 2026 release notes describe a reorderable left rail and a separate-window option for events. The notes list no ribbon changes. Your habits carry over, with new placement.
Privacy, confidential data and your employer's rules

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to produce an answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. These are product facts. They are not a statement about your employer's or university's rules.

blocks.title: Check before you hold the key
blocks.text: Restricted microdata, survey files covered by a data use agreement, and unpublished results may carry their own rules. Follow your institution's policy first. This page does not claim any compliance certification for any data.

A practical habit helps. Use Lazur for public data, your own drafts and questions about tools. For sensitive files, hide or close the window before you hold the key. Ask your data steward what counts as sensitive if the rules are unclear.
Common mistakes economists make with AI tools

items: Trusting a result because it looks neat. Lazur explains what is on screen. It does not check your model or your standard errors.
Pasting a citation without opening the paper. Open the source first, then check the claim.
Holding the wrong key. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about the screen. Hold fn to dictate text at the cursor.
Expecting Lazur to click. It guides one click at a time and waits. You do the clicking.
Dictating equations and not checking them. Voice input can mishear symbols, so read every line.
Skipping the Screen Time check. Without it, you cannot tell which task to hand off first.

blocks.text: Who this is for, and what it is not

Lazur is for Mac users on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, not available. It is not a plugin or add-in for Excel, Word or any other app. It has no partnership with any app maker, and it does not add features inside those apps.

It suits an economist who spends long days in Excel, Word, Mail and Stata and wants a voice for the small questions. It does not replace econometric training or the judgment a research question needs. Think of it as a sharp colleague who sits beside you.

faq.question: Is Lazur safe to use with confidential research data?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to produce an answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Those are Lazur's rules. Your data use agreement or employer policy may limit where data can go, so check it before you put that data on screen.

faq.question: Does Lazur work in Stata and Excel?
faq.answer: Lazur works in any app, because it sees the screen you are looking at. In Excel it can point at the PivotTable button or the Data tab. In Stata it can read an error message on screen and explain it. It does not run your do-file or edit your sheet.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Ask where a control is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do a task, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you.

faq.question: Is there a Windows version?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: Does Lazur cost money?
faq.answer: There is a trial that needs no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. Pro and Power plans are listed on the pricing page, with monthly and annual prices. Dictation is unlimited on both plans. Check the pricing page for current prices before you buy.

faq.question: Can I dictate a paper or a referee report with Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Snippets and a personal dictionary help with names, model labels and standard phrases. Read every result before you send it, because one wrong symbol can change a sentence's meaning.

faq.question: Does Lazur remember my work between sessions?
faq.answer: Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did. That memory is kept on your Mac. Use it to pick up a task from last week without starting over.

faq.question: Can Lazur check my regression code?
faq.answer: It can read code on screen and explain what a line does. It does not verify your identification strategy, your standard errors or your results. You decide whether the model is right, and you check the output yourself.

painPoints.title: Email eats the most hours
painPoints.text: The heaviest email users in Microsoft's 2023 study spent 8.8 hours a week on email. That is the top quarter of users, not an average economist. Still, email is the easiest block of time to win back.

painPoints.title: Communication takes most of the week
painPoints.text: Microsoft reports an average split of 57% communicating and 43% creating across workers. Economists are paid to create analysis and writing, so that split can feel wrong for your job.

painPoints.title: Data cleaning hides in plain sight
painPoints.text: The BLS says economists analyze data with models and software. Before any model runs, someone fixes dates, blanks and text numbers in Excel. That work rarely shows up in a job title.

painPoints.title: Switching between apps all morning
painPoints.text: A typical morning can move from Mail to Excel to Stata to Word and back. Each switch costs attention. Looking up a menu path or a Stata option adds more.

painPoints.title: Remembering where the menus moved
painPoints.text: Excel, Word and Outlook each hide common tasks in different places. Microsoft's release notes show frequent Outlook layout changes in 2026, so menus you learned last year may have moved.
